title: The Meeting That Started Before Everyone Could Arrive
title_ja: 全員が参加できる前に始まった住民会議
fact_notes: 町議会と住民の会議は架空の事例。実在の条例や司法判断は述べていない。本文・和訳・設問は独自制作。

sentences.en: A town council invites residents to discuss plans for renovating a public playground.
sentences.ja: 町の議会は公園の遊び場を改修する計画について住民を招いて話し合います。

sentences.en: The first meeting begins at four in the afternoon because the room is available then.
sentences.ja: 最初の会議は部屋が空いているため午後四時に始まります。

sentences.en: Most people attending are adults who do not work during those hours.
sentences.ja: 参加者の多くはその時間に働いていない大人です。

sentences.en: However, parents working late and students returning from school find it difficult to join.
sentences.ja: しかし遅くまで働く保護者や下校中の生徒には参加が難しいのです。

sentences.en: The council receives several messages asking whether those views can be included later.
sentences.ja: 議会にはその人々の意見を後で含められるか尋ねるメッセージが届きます。

sentences.en: The organizers realize that a public invitation does not guarantee an equal opportunity to speak.
sentences.ja: 主催者は公開の招待が話す機会の平等を保証しないと気づきます。

sentences.en: The council considers collecting comments through a website as an alternative to attending meetings.
sentences.ja: 議会は会議に参加する代わりにウェブサイトで意見を集めることを検討します。

sentences.en: For example, someone working in the afternoon could send a suggestion after returning home.
sentences.ja: 例えば午後に働く人は帰宅後に提案を送れるでしょう。

sentences.en: Yet the website may not work equally well for people with limited internet access.
sentences.ja: しかしインターネットを使いにくい人にはサイトが同じように役立つとは限りません。

sentences.en: Some residents prefer speaking directly, while others find writing less stressful.
sentences.ja: 直接話す方がよい住民もいれば書く方が気楽な住民もいます。

sentences.en: The council decides to compare several ways to receive information rather than selecting a single method immediately.
sentences.ja: 議会はすぐ一つの方法を選ぶのではなく複数の意見収集方法を比べると決めます。

sentences.en: It also asks how comments will be recorded and summarized fairly for later discussion.
sentences.ja: 意見が後の議論のため公平に記録され要約される方法も検討します。

sentences.en: A group of students suggests a short paper survey available at the library and community center.
sentences.ja: 生徒のグループは図書館と地域センターで使える短い紙の調査を提案します。

sentences.en: Instead of asking residents for unnecessary personal information, the questions focus on their experiences using the playground.
sentences.ja: 不必要な個人情報を尋ねず質問を遊び場の利用経験に絞ります。

sentences.en: The council also schedules a second meeting at a different time to make participation possible for more people.
sentences.ja: 議会はさらに多くの人が参加できるよう別の時刻に二回目の会議も予定します。

sentences.en: Students recognize that no arrangement will suit every person, but different options may reduce barriers.
sentences.ja: どの調整も全員に適するわけではないものの別の選択肢は障壁を減らすかもしれないと生徒は認識します。

sentences.en: They recommend explaining clearly when responses are due and how the council will use them.
sentences.ja: 回答の締切と議会がどう利用するかを明確に説明するよう勧めます。

sentences.en: The organizers agree to document important disagreements rather than hiding them in a single average opinion.
sentences.ja: 主催者は重要な意見の違いを平均的な一意見に隠さず記録すると合意します。

sentences.en: During the second meeting, residents hear a summary of comments collected through several routes.
sentences.ja: 二回目の会議では住民は複数の方法で集めた意見の要約を聞きます。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the council explains that these comments do not form a scientifically representative survey of the town.
sentences.ja: それでも議会は意見が町全体を科学的に代表する調査ではないと説明します。

sentences.en: The information can identify concerns, but it cannot prove that every resident supports the same proposal.
sentences.ja: 情報は懸念を特定できますが全住民が同じ提案を支持するとは証明できません。

sentences.en: Some parents prioritize safety, while teenagers ask for a place where older children can gather.
sentences.ja: 安全を優先する保護者もいれば年長の子どもが集まれる場所を求める十代の若者もいます。

sentences.en: The council discusses the limits of the budget and describes why some ideas may be difficult to implement.
sentences.ja: 議会は予算の限界を話し合い一部の考えが実施しにくい理由を説明します。

sentences.en: Participants find it easier to respond when they understand the reasons behind the decisions.
sentences.ja: 決定の背後の理由を理解すると参加者はより意見を述べやすくなります。

sentences.en: At the end of the process, the council publishes a short report describing the main options and unresolved questions.
sentences.ja: 過程の終わりに議会は主な選択肢と未解決の問いを説明する短い報告を公開します。

sentences.en: The report notes which suggestions affected the revised playground plan and which did not.
sentences.ja: 報告はどの提案が修正後の計画に影響しどれがしなかったか記します。

sentences.en: As a result, residents can understand how participation influenced the discussion even without universal agreement.
sentences.ja: その結果全員の合意がなくても参加が議論にどう影響したか住民は理解できます。

sentences.en: Students learn that democratic participation depends on more than sending invitations or counting comments.
sentences.ja: 生徒は民主的な参加が招待状の送付や意見数を数える以上のものに依存すると学びます。

sentences.en: A fair process should make room for different voices, explain its decisions, and admit what remains uncertain.
sentences.ja: 公平な過程は異なる声の余地を作り決定を説明し残る不明点を認めるべきです。

sentences.en: The community also learns that access to a meeting and influence over its outcome are related but not identical.
sentences.ja: 地域は会議へのアクセスと結果に影響することが関係しつつも同一ではないと学びます。

questions.prompt: Who has difficulty attending the first meeting?
options: Only people who live near the playground.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「しかし遅くまで働く保護者や下校中の生徒には参加が難しいのです。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What is the concern with the invitation?
options: An open invitation does not ensure equal chances to speak.
It automatically gives everyone a vote.
It prevents all residents from joining.
It cannot mention the meeting time.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「主催者は公開の招待が話す機会の平等を保証しないと気づきます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What limitation does the online option have?
options: It can only be used at the council office.
It guarantees that all opinions are identical.
It may exclude people with limited internet access.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「しかしインターネットを使いにくい人にはサイトが同じように役立つとは限りません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does the council consider beyond collecting comments?
options: Why the town has a playground.
How comments are recorded and summarized fairly.
Which resident has the most followers.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「意見が後の議論のため公平に記録され要約される方法も検討します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does the student survey focus on?
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「不必要な個人情報を尋ねず質問を遊び場の利用経験に絞ります。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: How will the organizers handle disagreements?
options: By recording important differences instead of hiding them.
By deleting views that do not match.
By reporting only one average opinion.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「主催者は重要な意見の違いを平均的な一意見に隠さず記録すると合意します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What limitation does the council acknowledge?
options: Every resident necessarily supports the plan.
The survey has no useful concerns.
The comments do not constitute a representative survey.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「情報は懸念を特定できますが全住民が同じ提案を支持するとは証明できません。」が根拠です。
第4段落「議会は予算の限界を話し合い一部の考えが実施しにくい理由を説明します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What can the final report help residents understand?
options: That meeting access is the only form of influence.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「その結果全員の合意がなくても参加が議論にどう影響したか住民は理解できます。」が根拠です。

options: Fair civic participation needs accessible routes, transparent decisions, and acknowledgment of limits.
One meeting time works for everyone.
Counting online comments automatically reveals public opinion.
Everyone must agree for a meeting to be democratic.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「地域は会議へのアクセスと結果に影響することが関係しつつも同一ではないと学びます。」が根拠です。
